course_title: Practical Exercise on European and Global Legal History
title: Exercise class 4: ius commune, usus modernus, common law, ius gentium

slides.title: Why the legend arose: the emperor as successor of the Caesars
slides.text: The exercise class explains WHAT the Lotharian legend grew out of, and that is a better answer than merely stating that it was untrue. THE ROMAN-GERMAN EMPERORS REGARDED THEMSELVES AS THE SUCCESSORS OF THE ANCIENT ROMAN CAESARS. From this it followed that THE CORPUS IURIS WAS INCREASINGLY REGARDED AS IMPERIAL LAW — the Codex Iustinianus was even, until the 14th century, EXPANDED WITH THE STATUTES OF THE ROMAN-GERMAN EMPERORS, that is, treated as an open collection of the ruler's own. In this atmosphere arose the LEGEND THAT THE EMPEROR LOTHAR III PUT THE CIC (BACK) INTO FORCE IN 1137. ITS FALSITY WAS DEMONSTRATED BY HERMANN CONRING (his De origine iuris Germanici appeared in 1643; an earlier version of the text is often dated 1632). AND THE EXERCISE ADDS A CONCLUSION WORTH REMEMBERING: PRECISELY FOR THIS EXPOSURE CONRING CAN BE REGARDED AS A PIONEER OF THE USUS MODERNUS PANDECTARUM. For whoever refutes the claim that Roman law applies by the emperor's command opens the question what actually does apply — and the answer of the usus modernus is: what practice actually uses, including native custom.

cards.q: What did the Lotharian legend grow out of?
cards.a: THE ROMAN-GERMAN EMPERORS REGARDED THEMSELVES AS THE SUCCESSORS OF THE ROMAN CAESARS, so THE CIC WAS INCREASINGLY REGARDED AS IMPERIAL LAW — the Codex Iustinianus was until the 14th century EXPANDED WITH THE STATUTES OF THE ROMAN-GERMAN EMPERORS. In that atmosphere arose the legend that THE EMPEROR LOTHAR III PUT THE CIC BACK INTO FORCE IN 1137.
cards.topic: The Ius Commune and the Early Modern Times

cards.q: Why is Conring a pioneer of the usus modernus pandectarum?
cards.a: Because whoever refutes that Roman law applies BY THE EMPEROR'S COMMAND opens the question WHAT ACTUALLY DOES APPLY — and the answer of the usus modernus is: WHAT PRACTICE ACTUALLY USES, INCLUDING NATIVE CUSTOM.
cards.topic: The Ius Commune and the Early Modern Times

slides.title: The usus modernus as the emancipation of native custom
slides.text: The exercise class defines the usus modernus differently from the usual account, and its definition is the more interesting one: THE USUS MODERNUS PANDECTARUM IS A SCHOLARLY SCHOOL OF THE 17TH CENTURY THAT CONTRIBUTED SIGNIFICANTLY TO THE EMANCIPATION OF NATIVE CUSTOMARY LAW. How? BY BEGINNING TO STUDY NATIVE CUSTOMARY LAW WITH THE SAME METHODS PREVIOUSLY USED FOR THE IUS COMMUNE. It is therefore not merely the 'practical use of the Pandects' — it is the ELEVATION OF NATIVE LAW INTO AN OBJECT WORTHY OF SCHOLARLY TREATMENT. THE RESULT IS A HYBRID OF THE IUS COMMUNE AND CUSTOMARY LAW, which in individual countries has its own name: IUS ROMANO-GERMANICUM in Germany, IUS ROMANO-HISPANICUM in Spain. Methodologically, Roman law was ADAPTED TO THE ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL CONDITIONS OF THE EARLY MODERN PERIOD and LOCAL LEGAL INSTITUTIONS AND CUSTOMS WERE MERGED WITH IT.

terms.def: A hybrid of the ius commune and native customary law; in Spain, correspondingly, ius Romano-Hispanicum.

cards.q: How does the exercise class define the usus modernus pandectarum, and why is that interesting?
cards.a: As a SCHOLARLY SCHOOL OF THE 17TH CENTURY THAT CONTRIBUTED SIGNIFICANTLY TO THE EMANCIPATION OF NATIVE CUSTOMARY LAW — by BEGINNING TO STUDY NATIVE CUSTOM WITH THE SAME METHODS PREVIOUSLY USED FOR THE IUS COMMUNE. It is therefore not merely the 'practical use of the Pandects' but the ELEVATION OF NATIVE LAW INTO AN OBJECT WORTHY OF SCHOLARSHIP. The result is a HYBRID: IUS ROMANO-GERMANICUM, in Spain IUS ROMANO-HISPANICUM.
cards.topic: The Ius Commune and the Early Modern Times

slides.title: The relation of humanism and the usus modernus, and the Dutch school
slides.text: The exercise class corrects the obvious oversimplification. METHODOLOGICALLY THE USUS MODERNUS WAS CLOSER TO THE MOS ITALICUS THAN TO LEGAL HUMANISM — because, like the commentators, it treated the text as an instrument for practice, not as a historical document. AND IT ADDS AT ONCE: THIS IS NOT A CONTRADICTION BUT RATHER A CROSS-POLLINATION. Many humanists also wrote practical treatises that can be assigned to the usus modernus; and in the practical literature, conversely, the findings of the humanists are reflected — for instance the question WHAT PLACE A GIVEN PASSAGE HAS IN THE CORPUS IURIS. THE DUTCH SCHOOL is evidence that the two could be combined: it was influenced by BOTH THE MOS GALLICUS AND THE USUS MODERNUS, and HUGO GROTIUS COMBINED THE DUTCH IURA PARTICULARIA WITH THE IUS COMMUNE. This is called ROMAN-DUTCH LAW; it spread to the Dutch colonies too and IS STILL IMPORTANT IN SOUTH AFRICA TODAY — a fine illustration of how long the reach of such a scholarly synthesis can be. THE SIGNIFICANCE OF THE USUS MODERNUS the exercise sums up in three points: (1) it was HIGHLY IMPORTANT FOR LEGAL PRACTICE UNTIL THE AGE OF CODIFICATIONS; (2) it CREATED THE METHODOLOGICAL STANDARDS UP TO THE 19TH CENTURY; (3) it CONSOLIDATED THE VALIDITY OF ROMAN LAW AND AT THE SAME TIME GAVE NATIVE LAW WEIGHT BY MERGING IT WITH IT — AND THEREBY PREPARED THE WAY FOR THE NATIONAL LEGAL ORDERS.

cards.q: Was the usus modernus closer to humanism or to the mos italicus?
cards.a: METHODOLOGICALLY IT WAS CLOSER TO THE MOS ITALICUS — like the commentators it treated the text as an INSTRUMENT FOR PRACTICE, not as a historical document. THIS IS NOT A CONTRADICTION BUT A CROSS-POLLINATION: humanists also wrote practical treatises, and the practical literature reflects humanist findings, such as the question what place a passage has in the CIC.
cards.topic: The Ius Commune and the Early Modern Times

cards.q: What did Grotius combine, and where does it still apply today?
cards.a: THE DUTCH IURA PARTICULARIA WITH THE IUS COMMUNE — the Dutch school was influenced by both the mos gallicus and the usus modernus. ROMAN-DUTCH LAW arose, spread to the Dutch colonies and IS STILL IMPORTANT IN SOUTH AFRICA TODAY.
cards.topic: The Ius Commune and the Early Modern Times

cards.q: Sum up the significance of the usus modernus pandectarum in three points.
cards.a: 1) It was HIGHLY IMPORTANT FOR PRACTICE UNTIL THE AGE OF CODIFICATIONS. 2) It CREATED THE METHODOLOGICAL STANDARDS UP TO THE 19TH CENTURY. 3) It CONSOLIDATED THE VALIDITY OF ROMAN LAW AND AT THE SAME TIME GAVE NATIVE LAW WEIGHT BY MERGING IT WITH IT — AND THEREBY PREPARED THE WAY FOR THE NATIONAL LEGAL ORDERS.
cards.topic: The Ius Commune and the Early Modern Times

slides.title: Reception through practice: the infiltration of Roman law
slides.text: The exercise class divides the reception into TWO ROUTES — LEGAL SCHOLARSHIP and LEGAL PRACTICE — and for practice it uses an expression worth remembering. THE GROWING NUMBER OF LEARNED JURISTS IN THE COURTS LED TO THE GRADUAL ACADEMIZATION OF LEGAL PRACTICE AND TO THE 'INFILTRATION OF ROMAN LAW'. It was therefore not a decision but a SEEPING IN. THE EXAMPLE IS THE IMPERIAL CHAMBER COURT — the supreme court of the Holy Roman Empire, founded IN 1495, where HALF THE MEMBERS WERE TO BE DOCTORS OF ROMAN LAW, and IN THE 16TH CENTURY LEGAL EDUCATION BECAME NECESSARY FOR ALL MEMBERS OF THE COURT. And its practice: IT APPLIED ROMAN LAW WHENEVER IT WAS UNCLEAR WHICH IURA PARTICULARIA WERE TO BE APPLIED OR WHAT THEY ACTUALLY PROVIDED. Note that this is not only about gaps: UNCERTAINTY ABOUT THE CONTENT of the local law was enough, and the learned law stepped in.

cards.q: How did Roman law assert itself through practice?
cards.a: THE GROWING NUMBER OF LEARNED JURISTS IN THE COURTS led to the GRADUAL ACADEMIZATION OF PRACTICE AND TO THE 'INFILTRATION OF ROMAN LAW' — it was not a decision but a SEEPING IN.
cards.topic: The Ius Commune and the Early Modern Times

cards.q: What was the composition of the Imperial Chamber Court and when did it apply Roman law?
cards.a: Founded in 1495; HALF THE MEMBERS WERE TO BE DOCTORS OF ROMAN LAW and IN THE 16TH CENTURY LEGAL EDUCATION BECAME NECESSARY FOR ALL. It applied Roman law WHENEVER IT WAS UNCLEAR WHICH IURA PARTICULARIA WERE TO BE APPLIED OR WHAT THEY ACTUALLY PROVIDED — so UNCERTAINTY ABOUT THE CONTENT of the local law was enough.
cards.topic: The Ius Commune and the Early Modern Times

slides.title: The Middle Ages: feudalism, manorial lordship and the lex familiae
slides.text: For the question about the road to state legislation the exercise class gives the starting position, which has to be described if the later development is to make sense. IN THE MIDDLE AGES THERE WERE HARDLY ANY STATUTES IN THE MODERN SENSE; CUSTOMARY LAW PREVAILED. The ruler issued statutes ONLY OCCASIONALLY AND WITH THE COOPERATION OF THE ESTATES, in order to suppress PARTICULAR ABUSES — that is, not to order a field of law but to drive away a concrete problem. FEUDALISM DOMINATED THE WHOLE OF THE MIDDLE AGES AND THE EARLY MODERN PERIOD: a FEUDAL LEGAL ORDER in which the rules of the LANDLORD apply, that is, MANORIAL LORDSHIP (GRUNDHERRSCHAFT): THE PEASANTS WERE DEPENDENT ON THE LORD PERSONALLY, IN PROPERTY AND POLITICALLY. Manorial lordship arose in the early Middle Ages FROM BOTH GERMANIC AND ROMAN LEGAL ROOTS. And on the estates a SPECIAL LEGAL SPHERE developed, the 'LEX FAMILIAE': THE LORD ACTED AS JUDGE — this is called PATRIMONIAL JURISDICTION. This matters for understanding everything that follows: as long as the lord judges and the law is customary, THERE IS NOBODY TO ISSUE STATUTES AND NOBODY FOR THEM TO BE ISSUED FOR.

terms.def: The special legal sphere of an estate, where the lord acts as judge (patrimonial jurisdiction).

cards.q: What did legislation look like in the Middle Ages?
cards.a: THERE WERE HARDLY ANY STATUTES IN THE MODERN SENSE; CUSTOMARY LAW PREVAILED. The ruler issued statutes ONLY OCCASIONALLY AND WITH THE COOPERATION OF THE ESTATES, in order to suppress PARTICULAR ABUSES — not to order a field of law but to drive away a concrete problem.
cards.topic: The Ius Commune and the Early Modern Times

cards.q: What is manorial lordship and the lex familiae?
cards.a: MANORIAL LORDSHIP (GRUNDHERRSCHAFT) is the feudal order in which THE PEASANTS ARE DEPENDENT ON THE LORD PERSONALLY, IN PROPERTY AND POLITICALLY; it arose from BOTH GERMANIC AND ROMAN ROOTS. The 'LEX FAMILIAE' is the special legal sphere of the estate, where THE LORD ACTS AS JUDGE — PATRIMONIAL JURISDICTION.
cards.topic: The Ius Commune and the Early Modern Times

slides.title: Three reasons why legislation increased from the 15th century
slides.text: The exercise class gives three reasons, all of them concrete, so they can be used directly in an answer. (1) THE TRANSITION FROM THE MIDDLE AGES TO THE MODERN PERIOD BROUGHT MANY PROBLEMS: economic crises (the NETHERLANDS and especially ENGLAND as newly rising powers), the FALL OF CONSTANTINOPLE and with it the DECLINE OF THE MEDITERRANEAN REGION (Venice), the DISCOVERY OF AMERICA. New problems needed new rules, and custom could not supply them fast enough. (2) THE RELIGIOUS WARS WEAKENED THE CHURCH AND THE TEMPORAL POWER TOOK OVER TASKS ORIGINALLY PERFORMED BY THE CHURCH — above all SOCIAL CARE. Whoever takes over a task must also regulate it. (3) THE CORPUS IURIS LED TO A CHANGED VIEW OF THE DUTIES OF PRINCES AND INSPIRED THEM TO BECOME LEGISLATORS THEMSELVES — for in the CIC they saw an emperor who issues statutes, and they wanted to be such too. AND THE PIONEERING ROLE BELONGED TO THE CITIES: THEY GAVE THEMSELVES MUNICIPAL LAW REFORMATIONS, strongly influenced by the CIC. Cities were smaller, denser and had a more urgent need for written rules than a territory as a whole.

cards.q: Which three reasons led to the growth of legislation from the 15th century?
cards.a: 1) THE TRANSITION TO THE MODERN PERIOD BROUGHT PROBLEMS: economic crises (the rise of the Netherlands and England), the FALL OF CONSTANTINOPLE and the decline of the Mediterranean, the DISCOVERY OF AMERICA. 2) THE RELIGIOUS WARS WEAKENED THE CHURCH and THE TEMPORAL POWER TOOK OVER ITS TASKS, above all SOCIAL CARE. 3) THE CIC CHANGED THE VIEW OF THE DUTIES OF PRINCES AND INSPIRED THEM TO BECOME LEGISLATORS. The pioneering role belonged to the CITIES with their LAW REFORMATIONS.
cards.topic: The Ius Commune and the Early Modern Times

slides.title: The dualism of the estates, and the fact that statutes were not exclusive
slides.text: OUT OF FEUDALISM CAME THE DUALIST STATE OF ESTATES: STATE POWER WAS SHARED BY TWO BODIES — THE RULER AND THE ASSEMBLY OF THE ESTATES. This is the arrangement out of which both absolutism (the ruler pushes the estates aside) and constitutionalism (the assembly turns into a parliament) will develop. IN THE HOLY ROMAN EMPIRE ONLY FEW IMPERIAL STATUTES CAME INTO BEING, because of the COMPLEX POLITICAL SITUATION — the example is the CONSTITUTIO CRIMINALIS CAROLINA, the criminal and criminal-procedure code of Charles V OF 1532. The CODEX MAXIMILIANEUS BAVARICUS CIVILIS, enacted IN 1756, can be regarded as THE LAST TERRITORIAL LAW REFORMATION AND AT THE SAME TIME AS A PRECURSOR OF THE NATURAL-LAW CODIFICATIONS — it stands exactly at the turn between the two epochs. AND A WARNING THE EXERCISE STRESSES EXPRESSLY AND WHICH IS EASILY OVERLOOKED: THESE STATUTES WERE NOT EXCLUSIVE — THEY REGULATED ONLY PARTICULAR LEGAL PROBLEMS, WHILE CUSTOMARY LAW CONTINUED TO BE APPLIED. It is precisely EXCLUSIVITY that will be the novelty brought only by the codifications.

cards.q: What is the dualist state of estates and what develops out of it?
cards.a: An arrangement in which STATE POWER IS SHARED BY TWO BODIES — THE RULER AND THE ASSEMBLY OF THE ESTATES. It came out of feudalism, and out of it develop both ABSOLUTISM (the ruler pushes the estates aside) and CONSTITUTIONALISM (the assembly turns into a parliament).
cards.topic: The Ius Commune and the Early Modern Times

cards.q: Were early modern statutes exclusive?
cards.a: NO — THEY REGULATED ONLY PARTICULAR LEGAL PROBLEMS, WHILE CUSTOMARY LAW CONTINUED TO BE APPLIED. It is precisely EXCLUSIVITY that will be the novelty brought only by the CODIFICATIONS. (Examples: the Carolina 1532; the CODEX MAXIMILIANEUS BAVARICUS CIVILIS 1756 as THE LAST TERRITORIAL LAW REFORMATION AND AT THE SAME TIME A PRECURSOR of the natural-law codifications.)
cards.topic: The Ius Commune and the Early Modern Times

slides.title: Public and private law: a division that never became one
slides.text: To the source from the Institutes the exercise class adds an analysis that runs against the way we usually read the sentence. ULPIAN'S FORMULA says that PUBLIC LAW (IUS PUBLICUM) CONCERNS 'THE ROMAN STATE', private law the benefit of the individual. BUT: A CATEGORICAL DIVISION INTO PRIVATE AND PUBLIC LAW WAS UNKNOWN IN THEORY AND IN PRACTICE ALIKE. It was a descriptive pair rather than a systemic boundary; what decided matters in practice was something else: THE SPECIAL RULE TOOK PRECEDENCE OVER THE MORE GENERAL ONE, and where a special rule was lacking, one reached for the 'IMPERIAL' or common law. IN THE MIDDLE AGES there already existed a distinction between the 'PUBLIC SPHERE' regulated by ius publicum and the 'PRIVATE SPHERE' of life, BUT THE BOUNDARIES BETWEEN THEM WERE ONLY PERCEPTIBLE, not sharp. And the key sentence: UNTIL THE PROCESSES OF STATE-BUILDING BEGAN IN THE EARLY MODERN PERIOD, THE TWO SPHERES WERE INSEPARABLE. Only when TERRITORIAL RULE asserted itself and the law of the territorial lord began to replace the existing order, and only with ABSOLUTISM, when the ruler became the LEGISLATOR AND THE DECISIVE CENTRAL FIGURE, did the division acquire a meaning. Incidentally, the content shifted as well: SACRAL LAW, ONCE PART OF THE IUS PUBLICUM, BECAME 'CHURCH LAW'.

cards.q: Did the division into private and public law exist in Rome?
cards.a: Ulpian's formula describes it, BUT A CATEGORICAL DIVISION WAS UNKNOWN IN THEORY AND PRACTICE ALIKE — it was a descriptive pair, not a systemic boundary. What decided matters in practice was something else: THE SPECIAL RULE TOOK PRECEDENCE OVER THE MORE GENERAL ONE, and where it was lacking, one reached for the common law.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

cards.q: When did the division into public and private law acquire a meaning?
cards.a: ONLY WITH THE PROCESSES OF STATE-BUILDING IN THE EARLY MODERN PERIOD — until they began, THE TWO SPHERES WERE INSEPARABLE. Only when TERRITORIAL RULE asserted itself and with ABSOLUTISM, when the ruler became the LEGISLATOR, did the division acquire content. The meaning shifted too: SACRAL LAW, once part of the ius publicum, became 'CHURCH LAW'.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

slides.title: Ius gentium in antiquity: the concrete content
slides.text: To the ius gentium the exercise class adds something the definitions lack — EXAMPLES. 'IUS GENTIUM' as the 'law common to all people' means ALL LEGAL PRINCIPLES THAT APPLY NOT ONLY TO ONE NATION BUT TO ALL NATIONS, and the exercise names two: THE INVIOLABILITY OF THE ENVOY and THE COMMON USE OF THE SEA SHORE. Note that both are in essence INTERNATIONAL — and yet in antiquity they were not assigned to a separate field. THOSE PRINCIPLES COMMON TO ALL PEOPLE WERE DERIVED IN ANTIQUITY FROM 'NATURE'. The IDEA OF JUSTICE played a key role here: CICERO IS THE FIRST TO MENTION THE DOCTRINE OF THE JUST WAR (BELLUM IUSTUM) — and for him a just war is a WAR OF DEFENCE AND A WAR TO AVENGE A WRONG SUFFERED. Typical of antiquity is also ARISTOTLE'S THINKING ON INTERNATIONAL LAW, which is SUFFUSED WITH NATURAL LAW and was REDISCOVERED IN THE EARLY MODERN PERIOD — precisely through late scholasticism and the School of Salamanca.

cards.q: Which concrete principles belonged to the ius gentium in antiquity?
cards.a: THE INVIOLABILITY OF THE ENVOY and THE COMMON USE OF THE SEA SHORE — principles applying NOT ONLY TO ONE NATION BUT TO ALL, derived from 'NATURE'. Both are in essence international, and yet they were not assigned to a separate field.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

cards.q: Who first mentions the doctrine of the just war, and what counts as one for him?
cards.a: CICERO. For him a just war is a WAR OF DEFENCE AND A WAR TO AVENGE A WRONG SUFFERED.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

slides.title: Ius gentium in the Middle Ages and its turn into ius inter gentes
slides.text: THE MIDDLE AGES WERE DOMINATED BY CHRISTIAN NATURAL-LAW THINKING — natural law has a DIVINE COMPONENT, God being the ground of everything. In the West ARISTOTLE was REDISCOVERED, and the typical expression of Christian natural law is the work of THOMAS AQUINAS. THE IUS GENTIUM IS GRADUALLY DESCRIBED AS THE LAW APPLIED AMONG CHRISTIAN RULERS AND COMMUNITIES — that is, a WESTERN COMMUNITY OF INTERNATIONAL LAW arises, headed by the ROMAN-GERMAN EMPEROR AS 'RULER OF THE WORLD' (so DANTE ALIGHIERI puts it in DE MONARCHIA, 1310) AND THE POPE AS THE SUPREME RULER OF CHRISTENDOM. THE LATE MIDDLE AGES: FROM ABOUT 1400 A EUROPEAN SYSTEM OF STATES BEGINS TO DEVELOP, FEUDAL STRUCTURES RECEDE AND INDEPENDENT 'STATES' INCREASINGLY ENTER INTO RELATIONS 'UNDER INTERNATIONAL LAW'. The ius gentium thus GRADUALLY TURNS INTO A LAW BETWEEN NATIONS — 'IUS INTER GENTES'. And the exercise adds a cause that is easily forgotten: A SIGNIFICANT LOSS OF PAPAL POWER WAS CAUSED BY THE WESTERN SCHISM (1378–1417); AFTER THE COUNCIL OF CONSTANCE IN 1417 THE POPES NEVER AGAIN ATTAINED THE POWER THEY HAD HELD IN THE MIDDLE AGES. Without the pope at the apex of the hierarchy, only a horizontal system of equals remained.

cards.q: How was the ius gentium understood in the Middle Ages?
cards.a: As the LAW APPLIED AMONG CHRISTIAN RULERS AND COMMUNITIES — a WESTERN COMMUNITY OF INTERNATIONAL LAW arises with the ROMAN-GERMAN EMPEROR AS 'RULER OF THE WORLD' (DANTE, DE MONARCHIA 1310) and the POPE AS SUPREME RULER OF CHRISTENDOM. All of it suffused with CHRISTIAN NATURAL-LAW THINKING (Thomas Aquinas).
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

cards.q: When and why does the ius gentium become ius inter gentes?
cards.a: FROM ABOUT 1400: a EUROPEAN SYSTEM OF STATES develops, FEUDAL STRUCTURES RECEDE and independent states enter into relations under international law. The LOSS OF PAPAL POWER THROUGH THE WESTERN SCHISM (1378–1417) contributed — AFTER THE COUNCIL OF CONSTANCE IN 1417 THE POPES NEVER REGAINED THAT POWER. Without the pope at the apex, a HORIZONTAL SYSTEM OF EQUALS remained.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

slides.title: The 'Spanish era' 1500–1648
slides.text: The exercise class names the whole period of international law after its leading power and gives it a frame. IN 1453 THE BYZANTINE EMPIRE ENDS; OUT OF THE MUSCOVITE STATE THE RUSSIAN EMPIRE ARISES, soon to take the LEADING ROLE IN THE ORTHODOX WORLD. In the territory of former Byzantium the OTTOMAN EMPIRE emerges — VIENNA WAS TWICE BESIEGED FOR SEVERAL MONTHS, IN 1529 AND 1683. IN THE 15TH CENTURY THE ERA OF COLONIZATION BEGINS, carried by SPAIN AND PORTUGAL: IN 1492 THE DISCOVERY OF AMERICA and IN THE SAME YEAR THE EXPULSION OF THE MUSLIMS FROM EUROPE BY THE CONQUEST OF GRANADA, that is, the END OF THE RECONQUISTA. In central Europe the Spanish era is marked by RELIGIOUS CONFLICTS. THIS CONNECTION IS THE POINT: THE SAME PERIOD THAT BROUGHT OVERSEAS EXPANSION ALSO BROUGHT THE RELIGIOUS WARS IN EUROPE — and international law is born out of both at once. From overseas come questions about titles to foreign land and about the standing of other peoples (Vitoria, Salamanca); from Europe the question how rulers of different denominations are to live together. The two intersect in 1648.

cards.q: What defines the 'Spanish era' of international law (1500–1648)?
cards.a: 1453 THE END OF BYZANTIUM — out of Muscovy arises the RUSSIAN EMPIRE with the leading role in the Orthodox world, and in Byzantine territory the OTTOMAN EMPIRE emerges (Vienna besieged in 1529 and 1683). In the 15th century the ERA OF COLONIZATION by Spain and Portugal begins: 1492 THE DISCOVERY OF AMERICA and IN THE SAME YEAR THE END OF THE RECONQUISTA with the conquest of Granada. In central Europe, RELIGIOUS CONFLICTS.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

cards.q: Out of what is modern international law born?
cards.a: OUT OF BOTH AT ONCE: from OVERSEAS EXPANSION come questions about TITLES TO FOREIGN LAND and the standing of other peoples (Vitoria, Salamanca); from EUROPE the question HOW RULERS OF DIFFERENT DENOMINATIONS ARE TO LIVE TOGETHER. The two intersect IN 1648.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism
